purpose: Carry forward the already-accepted submarine information-age/contact-handoff rules into the Central Pacific mobilization warning, rather than treating submarines only as torpedo platforms.

authoritative_internal_rules.content: standard contact reports contain time/position/enemy type/course/speed/confidence/own state; reports age and submerged boats do not receive a modern continuous data link
headquarters fuses multiple submarine reports with base air, traffic analysis and DF into enemy probability corridors and issues next patrol line/time
a boat may preserve/shadow/report a high-value carrier/battleship contact instead of taking a low-quality shot
Branch survival and status discipline reduce historical dead-node / silent-node / paper-roster ambiguity, making a missing report less likely to be an unknowable sunk-vs-radio-failure case
fresh external information improves intercept/recontact probability but never creates an automatic firing solution or wolfpack real-time data link

layers.mission: Hawaii/Gilberts/central-Pacific approach and oiler/transport traffic; report first, attack selectively
probable carrier/assault/oiler transit corridors and Majuro/Kwajalein outer approaches
convert dated outer reports into 10-20 nmi intercept corrections; sprint then slow/relisten, not continuous 19-kt pursuit

jan28_assignment.named_anchor: I-175 repair return band closes by mid-Jan and it can re-enter Central Pacific patrol allocation; exact remaining conventional names are deliberately not invented without dated patrol traces.
jan28_assignment.opportunity_cost: The 7-boat Indian Ocean active/outbound layer is preserved; Marshall concentration uses the much larger Pacific-ready pool and does not silently cancel the already-realized western response.

realized_warning_effect_through_28Jan.event: Submarine/traffic/DF picture detects elevated escorted logistics and naval traffic toward the Gilbert-Central Pacific axis; no carrier identity.

At least one outer reporting boat obtains a timed visual/periscope or hydrophone-assisted surface contact on escorted auxiliary/transport traffic and transmits a structured report; attack is not required for the information to count.
A second independent submarine-sector report plus US land-air suppression tempo and DF/traffic changes allow headquarters to shift Marshall air search arcs and inner submarine patrol lines.
realized_warning_effect_through_28Jan.Japan_confidence: HIGH major Central-Pacific operation; MEDIUM-HIGH Marshalls target

realized_warning_effect_through_28Jan.event: No weapon-quality carrier track is credited yet. The contact network nevertheless makes 'operation imminent in days, not weeks' HIGH confidence and reduces the risk that a missed air scout resets the picture to zero.
realized_warning_effect_through_28Jan.Japan_confidence: HIGH imminent; exact Kwajalein vs outer-atoll objective remains MEDIUM

quantified_operational_payoff.warning: moves the Japanese warning state up roughly one evidence rung before firm air visual contact when two independent dated reports correlate with DF/traffic/land-air indicators
quantified_operational_payoff.search: permits the 6-8 useful daily long-range searches to concentrate on probability corridors and reserves 1-2 faster confirmation sorties for suspicious contacts
quantified_operational_payoff.intercept: Sentaka receives time-stamped intercept geometry rather than a generic patrol box; usefulness collapses as report age grows
quantified_operational_payoff.fleet_gate: submarine warning can raise readiness/dispersal and start search/repositioning, but cannot by itself open the Japanese first-line-carrier strike gate

anti_double_count: Do not add a generic submarine hit bonus on top of this information effect.
Do not count one contact report again as independent DF evidence.
Do not turn a non-attack report into an invisible torpedo opportunity.
Do not infer carrier identity from oiler/transport traffic alone.
